changes.reason: Connect labelled four-status selector, result counts and loading/error/empty rows to independent project selection using existing API and UI helpers.
Own asynchronous filter/selection state; preserve selection on loading, empty and failure; guard stale responses; retry current status.
Add wrapping reference toolbar and labelled-control spacing with existing space token while keeping blue and responsive tokens/styles.
Cover filtered data, preserved selection, current-filter retry, distinct request states and stale success/failure suppression.

requirements.reason: Status selector uses all four values; existing projects client receives selection; successful row count and rows render from returned result. Actual browser showed 3/2/1/0 for All/Active/Archived/Paused.

Selection lives separately from visible projects, panel always reflects selected name, empty is a distinct success branch, selected ID is passed to existing renderRows. Browser Tide remained selected while hidden and empty then returned pressed.

Errors use existing showProblem and Retry callback; default load status is the current filter and selection is not reset. Browser failure at Paused stayed distinct from empty; after recovery Retry returned 0 and retained Tide.

Dedicated loading message and busy flag preserve selected panel. Both successful and failed stale responses are ignored by request ID. Browser loading observed and rapid Active then Archived settled to Forest; unit tests cover both stale outcomes.

Uses unchanged selectField/renderRows/showProblem and API client; selected reference toolbar uses app blue/system space values. Actual 1280 wide split, 375 narrow stack, no overflow and 3px blue keyboard focus were observed.

verification.detail: npm test passed 5 tests: API status/rejection; filter-selection-empty; loading/error/current-filter retry; stale success; stale failure. No skipped tests.

Actual app displayed visible Status combobox with All/Active/Archived/Paused and 3/2/1/0 matching rows. Request paths are traced through unchanged src/api.js, and live loopback GET URL/status/count checks passed. Direct browser performance/network timing inspection was unavailable, retained honestly in tool-limit evidence.
